recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed unless the Security WG separately decides to revise the Extension Pack definition, such as narrowing or documenting the extra RelatedPerson target that is broader than the original Jira text but not inconsistent with the on-behalf-of concept.
issue_request: FHIR-40293 was a Published Security WG change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, requesting a core extension allowed on AuditEvent.agent: agent-onbehalfOf 0..1 Reference to Organization, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, CareTeam, or Patient.
initial_application: No Jira-keyed FHIR core commit was found for FHIR-40293 and current core has no duplicate auditevent-OnBehalfOf definition. The apparent application is HL7/fhir-extensions commit 71471775152ef25e4e333d4d6ead80c3df7a4741, which added StructureDefinition-auditevent-OnBehalfOf.xml with context AuditEvent.agent, max 1, and Reference targets covering the requested resources plus RelatedPerson.
additional_context: Security WG minutes from 2023-02-13 record approval of option 4, the extension approach, by a 6-0-0 vote. Current FHIR core history states that all extensions moved to hl7.fhir.uv.extensions and are still published as part of the specification, making the Extension Pack the current authoritative source for this extension. Later Extension Pack maintenance changed metadata but preserved the extension semantics.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit on the combined branch and made no source changes. The current core AuditEvent resource is active, but the requested extension is already present in the Extension Pack with the approved AuditEvent.agent context and cardinality, so duplicating it in core or adding redundant core prose would be inconsistent with current source organization.

related_jiras.note: Later Extension Pack maintenance changed auditevent-OnBehalfOf metadata to non-experimental but did not change the FHIR-40293 semantics.
